I will think this through the way I always do — starting from what worked last year and adjusting a little.

My 11.4 mu is split like this: 9.4 mu for the wheat-maize rotation (two crops on the same ground, the way we always do it here in Quzhou), and 2 mu I keep for cotton on the sandier corner where wheat does not grow so well. Cotton prices are not what they used to be, but I have grown it for years and the land suits it.

**Winter wheat (9.4 mu):** I will plant Jimai 22 again — it did well for my neighbor Old Wang last year, about 520 kg/mu. I sow around October 10, about 15 kg seed per mu. For fertilizer I put down 50 kg of diammonium phosphate per mu before plowing (that gives me roughly 9 kg N and 23 kg P2O5, so 10 kg P), then topdress 25 kg urea per mu at jointing in spring — that is another 11-12 kg N. Total about 20 kg N. I add one bag of potassium sulfate across the plot, roughly 7 kg K per mu. Irrigate three times: winter water in December, jointing water in April, grouting water in May. Two sprays — one herbicide for wild oats in early spring, one mixed spray for aphids and powdery mildew in May. Rotary tillage after maize is cleared, it is faster and the kids are not around to help.

**Summer maize (9.4 mu):** Straight after wheat harvest in June, no plowing — direct seed Zhengdan 958 with the seeder, about 2.5 kg/mu. I put compound fertilizer 15-15-15 at 40 kg/mu in the furrow (that's 6 kg each of N, P, K), then top-dress 26 kg urea at the big trumpet stage — so total about 18 kg N, 6 kg P, 5 kg K. Irrigate twice if the rain is short — once after sowing if dry, once at tasseling. Spray twice: one for armyworm around knee-high, one for corn borer. I expect 550 kg/mu, same as last year.

**Cotton (2 mu):** Bt hybrid seed from the dealer in the county town — Bt still does not stop the aphids and mirids, only the bollworm. Plough deep before planting in late April. Base fertilizer 40 kg compound (15-15-15) plus 15 kg urea — gives me about 13 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. I top-dress another 10 kg urea at flowering, so about 17 kg N total — I round it to 15 because my soil is not poor. Add 10 kg potassium sulfate, that's another 4 kg K, call it 8. Cotton drinks water — three irrigations: before planting, at budding, at flowering. Spray six times through the summer for aphids, mirids, spider mites — that is the worst part of cotton, the spraying never stops. Yield maybe 250 kg seed cotton per mu, if the weather holds.

I spend a bit more on fertilizer than some people say is needed. My thinking is simple: if I short the fertilizer and the yield drops 50 kg, I lose far more than the 30-40 yuan I saved. Better to put a little extra.
